definitions.explanation: Going beyond what is appropriate or reasonable. Used to describe behavior, amounts, or conditions that exceed healthy or acceptable limits.

examples.japanese: {過度|かど}な{飲酒|いんしゅ}は{体|からだ}に{悪|わる}い。
examples.english: Excessive drinking is bad for the body.

examples.japanese: {過度|かど}なストレスが{病気|びょうき}の{原因|げんいん}になった。
examples.english: Excessive stress was the cause of the illness.

examples.japanese: {過度|かど}な{期待|きたい}をかけると、{子|こ}どもにプレッシャーを{与|あた}えてしまう。
examples.english: Placing excessive expectations on children puts pressure on them.

notes:
USAGE:
{過度|かど} is almost always used as a modifier with な, describing something that goes beyond reasonable limits. It is formal in tone and common in medical, health, and policy writing.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {過度|かど}な + noun (excessive...)
- {過度|かど}に + verb/adjective (excessively...)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {過度|かど}なストレス (excessive stress)
- {過度|かど}な{飲酒|いんしゅ} (excessive drinking)
- {過度|かど}な{運動|うんどう} (excessive exercise)
- {過度|かど}な{期待|きたい} (excessive expectations)
- {過度|かど}な{心配|しんぱい} (excessive worry)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{過剰|かじょう} (surplus, excess) emphasizes having too much of something. {過度|かど} emphasizes that the degree or extent has gone too far.
